findings.facts: HTTP factories fix the exact Development host and allowlisted paths/methods. The PostgreSQL observer fixes its pooler route, project-qualified user, port and database. There is no alternate Production destination in these factories.

findings.scope: Native factory options, not a live handshake
findings.facts: Both reviewed HTTPS factories explicitly enable peer verification and set the Development TLS servername, with agent:false and no redirects. They use Node HTTPS certificate/hostname verification rather than an insecure fallback. HTTP trust uses the Node trust configuration, not the pinned PostgreSQL CA bytes.

findings.scope: Fixed observer factory options and pinned CA-byte check only
findings.facts: Observer requires memory-provided CA bytes matching the fixed approved SHA-256, uses rejectUnauthorized:true, explicit servername and checkServerIdentity. The recorded verify-full requirement is implemented by these TLS options; no verify-ca/insecure fallback is configured.

No handshake, DNS/endpoint observation, current certificate-chain validation or credential-channel check occurred. Source pins and historical CA references do not establish the current session identity. A shared pooler certificate is not project identity proof by itself.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Keep the live safeguard UNVERIFIED until a separately authorized exact-target connection receipt establishes hostname/chain validation, project routing and protected credential transport; do not connect under this offline check.

findings.scope: Input helper source and injected terminal tests only
findings.facts: Input is explicit, hidden and bounded to at most 180 seconds; non-TTY input, competing readers, cancellation/EOF/error and timeout fail closed. Imports do not prompt or retrieve secrets.

findings.scope: Reviewed credential and transport modules only
findings.facts: No environment/argv/file/secret-store credential lookup or credential-file write exists in the reviewed ports. Required providers explicitly supply memory values. Disposal clears retained references and invalidates handles, but cannot zeroize previous strings, copies or operating-system buffers.

findings.scope: Exact reviewed modules and synthetic error/diagnostic tests only
findings.facts: Credential handles redact default JSON/inspection; transport failures use fixed sanitized messages and source has no request/body/credential logging sink. Deliberate extraction/spreading, external middleware, debugging or provider logs can still expose plaintext. Intentional wire serialization contains credentials in memory and is not a persistence guarantee.

findings.scope: Configured cooperative asynchronous source bounds and injected tests
findings.facts: HTTP timers are 7s; Auth creation and session bootstrap phases 30s; Admin absence callback/body parsing 2s; mapping confirmation 2s. Observer has 2s connect, 5s query/statement, 2s lock, 10s idle transaction and 20s general/2s mapping capture bounds, including close checks. Abort signals propagate and failures close/destroy clients. TTY input has its separate <=180s ceiling.

Create and provisioning attempts are one-shot; observer checkpoints are consumed; uncertain writes stop forward mutations in explicit state mode. There is no transport retry, refresh fallback or automatic compensation. Client destruction/cancellation/expiry and stable snapshots do not prove backend termination or rollback, and restarting a process is not retry authority.

findings.scope: Source/test evidence exists; actual protected process and hard deadline evidence missing
findings.facts: JavaScript timers/Promise races depend on event-loop scheduling and are not an external hard process deadline or backend drain proof. Injected send/clientFactory/requestImpl ports must be composed with the reviewed native adapters; arbitrary or preloaded replacements can defeat source assumptions. Actual debugger/preload/transcription/request logging, trust-store overrides, executable/dependency integrity and credential custody remain unverified. Check9 logging clearance remains BLOCKED.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Owner supplies a non-secret, reviewable launch/runtime safeguard record for the intended dedicated execution process: exact reviewed entrypoint/adapters and hashes, debugger/preload/transcription/body logging disabled, and the configured overall-deadline mechanism. Do not enter credentials or make a connection.

findings.scope: Offline renderer/template and state guards, not an executed or authorized cleanup
findings.facts: renderCleanup validates exact IDs/counts and an explicit privileged-bypass acknowledgement. The SERIALIZABLE template locks identity tables/rows, checks wrapper absence/original RPC denial, dependencies, Auth presence and exact mappings, then deletes links before canonical users with affected-row assertions. It deliberately bypasses RLS administratively; the rendering boolean is not approval. State mode requires separately bound Gate4 approval/ownership/dependency evidence and blocks unresolved UNKNOWN. No Auth users are deleted by this SQL.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Before any separately authorized Gate4 cleanup, bind actual independently observed owned canonical IDs, exact Auth presence, dependency/privilege evidence, rendered artifact hash and explicit administrative RLS-bypass/lock-impact approval; do not render or execute it here.
